approval.note: Plan acceptance is 'onboards without product-code or contract-schema changes'; the other gates are the implementing agent's proposals. Not approved.

manual_steps: The data owner reviews the imported draft: ownership, descriptions, grain, and the metric definition.
A human adds policies (allowed purposes, classification, required filters); an import carries none, so nothing is answerable without them.
Semantic certification (lifecycle and metric) by the certifying owner, in the Git-backed registry; the drill's sandbox flip is not this.
A context snapshot, ontology labels/aliases, and a physical data source and gateway for the tenant are provisioned.
The scripted model of the reference stack knows only the first tenant's phrasings; a real model with the tenant's context is needed for natural-language questions.

not_measured.natural_language_for_tenant_b: the drill compiles and runs an intent; the reference stack's scripted model only understands the first tenant, so end-to-end natural-language onboarding is not shown
not_measured.policy_authoring: an imported model has no policies; authoring and reviewing them is manual and not evaluated
not_measured.real_ossie_models: one small hand-written model in the pinned 0.2.0.dev0 subset; real-world Ossie documents, other versions, and lossy constructs beyond metric expressions are not exercised
not_measured.live_warehouse: a local Parquet file stands in for the tenant's warehouse
not_measured.identity_and_groups: the second tenant's identity provider mapping is not onboarded
not_measured.export_of_metrics: Ossie export carries datasets and fields only (the ADS-008 subset): metrics and time-dimension flags are not exported, so a round trip is not lossless. Whether export should carry metrics is a decision for the user; it would not change the Compass contract schema.
